title: user_details view lost security_invoker, exposing every user's PII to any authenticated user
root_cause: 20260304100000 DROPs and re-CREATEs public.user_details without WITH (security_invoker = true), then GRANTs SELECT to authenticated. A Postgres view without security_invoker executes with the view owner's privileges, so RLS on public.profiles is bypassed. This is the last migration touching the view, so it is the current effective state. The same regression happened once before: set at 20260113000000:104, lost, restored at 20260226000000:19, and lost again here.
entrypoint: any authenticated Supabase client: select * from user_details
sink: every row of profiles joined to gamification_profiles: email, full_name, student_id, faculty, course, year, avatar_url, xp
verification: RED without the migration: test named 4 exposed views including public.user_details. GREEN with it. Full gate 1112/1112, typecheck, lint, secrets clean. NOT APPLIED to any database - the migration is committed but unrun, so the production exposure REMAINS until it is deployed.
deployment_impact: LIVE IN PRODUCTION. Requires a database migration to fix; cannot be resolved by a code deploy.
notes: VERIFIED BY ME by reading the migration chronology, not taken on the subagent's word. Attacker capability required is only a valid authenticated session - i.e. any registered student - which is why this is P0 and not P1. Fix is one statement: ALTER VIEW public.user_details SET (security_invoker = true); shipped as a new idempotent migration, plus a regression test. title: WebAuthn challenge consumption is not atomic and its delete result is unchecked
root_cause: consumeChallenge() performs SELECT then a separate DELETE. Two callers can both pass the SELECT before either DELETE commits. The DELETE result is discarded, so a failed delete silently leaves the challenge valid until its 5-minute expiry.
sink: webauthn_challenges table; session establishment via admin magic link
verification: Reproduction RED: two concurrent consumers both claimed one challenge (expected 1, got 2). GREEN after fix. Siblings green (webauthn-auth-options, webauthn-credentials 17/17). Full suite 1110/1110, typecheck clean, lint clean, format clean.
deployment_impact: Live in production since the 2026-07-29 Cloudflare cutover. No deployment change required to fix; code-only.
notes: Defence-in-depth is incomplete: @simplewebauthn only enforces the signature counter when the stored counter is > 0, and synced platform passkeys (iCloud Keychain, Google Password Manager) commonly report 0, which skips that check. updateCredentialCounter() also writes newCounter unconditionally with no monotonic guard and only logs errors. For counter-0 authenticators the challenge delete is therefore the sole single-use guarantee. Attacker capability required: possession of a valid unexpired assertion, so not trivially exploitable - hence P2 not P1. Fix: single atomic DELETE ... WHERE challenge/type/not-expired RETURNING *, plus a monotonic guard on the counter update.

title: Unverified client-supplied WebAuthn public key is later trusted to mint a session
root_cause: POST /api/auth/biometric writes client-supplied credentialId and publicKey straight into user_metadata with no WebAuthn registration ceremony - no challenge, no attestation, no proof of possession. authenticate/verify then reads biometric_public_key back as legacyPublicKey and passes it to verifyAuthenticationResponse as the trusted credential public key.
sink: session issued via admin magic link for the victim user_id
verification: RED confirmed against pre-fix code via git stash: POST /api/auth/biometric with enabled:true and attacker-supplied credentialId/publicKey crashed (500) rather than being rejected, and would have written the attacker-controlled key into user_metadata. GREEN after fix: endpoint now rejects enabled:true with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR before touching auth.updateUser() or webauthn_credentials; credentialId/publicKey/counter/transports removed from the accepted schema entirely. Confirmed the only two real frontend callers of POST /api/auth/biometric (lib/hooks/useBiometrics.ts) are the status GET and the enabled:false disable call - the vulnerable enabled:true+credential path was dead weight for legitimate users, so no real user flow is broken. Legitimate enrollment already goes through the verified ceremony at /api/auth/passkey/register-options + /api/auth/passkey/register (verifyRegistrationResponse against a server-issued, cookie-bound challenge), which is untouched and remains the only way biometric_public_key/biometric_credential_id can be written. Full suite green, typecheck clean.
deployment_impact: Live in production since the 2026-07-29 cutover. Code-only fix.
notes: VERIFIED BY ME against source, not taken from the subagent report. Attacker plants their own public key, holds the matching private key, and the signature verifies. Required capability: an authenticated session on the victim account (XSS, stolen cookie, or borrowed device) - so not P0. Impact is persistence: converts a temporary compromise into a permanent password-independent backdoor that survives a password reset, and per the reported BA-0005 other sessions are not revoked on password change either. Fix: stop trusting user_metadata credential material for authentication; require a real registration ceremony writing to webauthn_credentials, and retire the legacy metadata path or gate it behind proof of possession. FIXED BY ME: closed the unverified write path in app/api/auth/biometric/route.ts rather than tearing out the whole legacy user_metadata credential system, because app/api/auth/passkey/register already performs a real WebAuthn registration ceremony against that same metadata and is actively used by real legacy passkey holders - retiring it wholesale would have broken them. authenticate/verify's trust of biometric_public_key is now safe because that field can only be populated via a verified ceremony.

title: WebAuthn RP ID and expected origin fall back to client-controlled Host/Origin headers
root_cause: getRelyingPartyId(host) returns host.split(':')[0] and getExpectedOrigin(requestOrigin) returns requestOrigin when WEBAUTHN_RP_ID / WEBAUTHN_ORIGIN are unset. Both inputs come from request headers.

It remains a fail-open shape: any environment that loses those vars silently derives WebAuthn's two anchoring values from attacker-controlled headers, defeating origin binding entirely. Fix: fail closed when the env vars are absent instead of falling back to headers.

title: Reported: push subscription upsert on globally-unique endpoint via admin client can reassign another user's subscription
root_cause: app/api/push/subscription/route.ts:23 used `createAdminClient() ?? title: P1: gamification_profiles self-service XP tampering; on_deadline_completed double XP by toggling completed; schedule_members UPDATE permitting reassignment to arbitrary users/roles
root_cause: Three independent gaps, all USING-only RLS policies or missing table-level revokes: (a) gamification_profiles UPDATE policy checks only auth.uid()=user_id, not which columns change, and INSERT/UPDATE remain GRANTed to authenticated even after 20260214000000 hardened the RPC functions but not the table grant; (b) on_deadline_completed() has no idempotency guard and xp_events had no UNIQUE constraint, so toggling deadlines.completed false/true re-earns XP; (c) 'Schedule owners can update members' (20260220100000_realtime_offline.sql) has no WITH CHECK, so user_id/role are unconstrained on the new row.
entrypoint: (a) supabase.from('gamification_profiles').update({xp:...}); (b) repeated toggling of deadlines.completed via the normal API; (c) supabase.from('schedule_members').update({user_id, role})
control: (a) none beyond row ownership; (b) none; (c) row ownership of the parent schedule only, no column-level check
sink: (a) gamification_profiles.xp/streak_days/longest_streak; (b) xp_events + gamification_profiles.xp via duplicate award_xp() calls; (c) schedule_members.user_id/role for an arbitrary target row
verification: RED without the migration across all three sub-findings: authenticated still held INSERT/UPDATE on gamification_profiles, award_xp() had no already_awarded guard and no unique index existed, and the schedule_members update policy had no WITH CHECK / no reassignment trigger. GREEN with 20260729090300_fix_gamification_and_schedule_tampering.sql. Full test suite 1128/1128, typecheck clean, lint clean. NOT APPLIED to any database.
deployment_impact: Live in production. Requires a database migration to fix; cannot be resolved by a code deploy.
deferred_reason: Awaiting independent verification against source before triage.
notes: VERIFIED BY ME against the migration chain for all three sub-parts. Fix (a) revokes INSERT/UPDATE from authenticated (award_xp/update_streak are SECURITY DEFINER and run as table owner, unaffected); (b) adds a UNIQUE index on xp_events(user_id,event_type,reference_id) plus an already_awarded short-circuit in award_xp(); (c) adds WITH CHECK blocking role='owner' plus a BEFORE UPDATE trigger blocking user_id reassignment outside service_role, since RLS predicates alone cannot compare OLD vs NEW columns.

title: Reported: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW IF NOT EXISTS silently no-ops, so a later migration's richer matview schema was never applied
root_cause: Claimed: 20260114000000 creates mv_deadline_analytics with a narrower column set; 20260114013519 then uses CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW IF NOT EXISTS, which does not replace an existing definition, so the intended week_start/priority/type columns were never added. The following CREATE UNIQUE INDEX on those columns would then fail on a fresh replay.
deployment_impact: If true, the migration chain is not replayable from scratch - relevant to disaster recovery and to standing up any staging database.
deferred_reason: Awaiting independent verification.
notes: Observation originated from the Lane D subagent, which attempted to fix it by EDITING the already-applied historical migration in the main worktree and inserting DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW statements. That edit was reverted; main is clean. Editing an applied migration is not an acceptable fix - the file would no longer match what ran against production, and the added DROPs would destroy those views on replay. The underlying observation may still be valid and is worth verifying, but any fix must be a NEW forward migration. The reverted diff is kept at proposed-migrations/REVERTED-main-edit.patch for reference only.
